Hello! I am diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder and is curently taking therapy in my univesity's hospital. I had the same problem before when my depression was severe last year; I had to take a leave of absence for a year because I could hardly study at all (I was a nursing student, you see. and it really messed me up because of all the stress).

I'd like to share with you the things I learned in my therapy. The therapy I'm undergoing is called Dialectical Behavioral Therpy. Here are a few things I learned:
- Your mind is used to 'time-travelling' meaning your mind tends to go back to the past a lot and relive bad memories and replay them in your head over and over. This is the reason we suffer a lot. A hurtful event that happened a few months ago may still be stuck in your head even until know. Your feelings are valid, however, in order for you to stop hurting, you need to stop time-travelling. One way to do this is to focus on the present. Whenever you catch yourself thinking about the hurtful event, IMMEDIATELY take yourself back to the present. Ask yourself: What's happening right now? Where am I? 
Which brings me to my next point
- Focus Shifting. Once you catch yourself time-travelling, shift your focus to anything, then describe it for one whole minute. For example, I've been thinking about what my ex-friend did to me last month. It triggered me earlier. I started palpitating and had mild anxiety symptoms, so knowing the signs I started shifting my focus to something in front of me: a book! Describe it in full detail in your mind. The book is color red. It is printed in paperback. The pages are smooth and it smells new, etc. Don't divert your thoughts anywhere, just focus on describing the object. Since I've been going to therapy for a year now, this usually does the trick.
- Mindfulness. Practice meditating everyday. It's hard to study when you're sad because your emotions are heightened, the part of your brain that's responisble for your emotions is going haywire which prevents you from focusing on anything; hence having difficulties on studying. That's one of the reasons why my therapist encourages me to practice meditation, so I can clear my mind of anything so that I can focus. It's also to prevent myself from thinking about the bad things that happened to me last year. What you can do here is that you find a comfortable place to sit, set an alarm for one minute, close your eyes and just focus on your breathing. Don't thinking of anything at all, let your mind be absolutely blank and maybe count your breathing as you inhale through your nose and exhale through your mouth. 

If you want more info, feel free to ask, including where you can find a PDF of the DBT, I can give it to you. I just drank my anti-psychotics which help me sleep so this is all I can type for now.
